table

10. Elements of same

period are given below: a. Identify the period. Why are these elements kept in the same period? b. What is the meaning of the different colors of the elements given? c. Why is there a gap between magnesium and aluminum? d. Name the elements that have metallic and covalent radius.
11. Energy change while adding electrons in the fluorine atom is given.
F(g) + e → F- (g) Energy = -328 kJ /mol
a. Name the energy and define it. b. What do you mean by the negative value of energy in the given equation? c. Will the value of energy be higher or lower than fluorine if the above case is
applied for nitrogen?

18. Effective nuclear charge is the net resultant charge of the nucleus which is a very useful parameter to explain the periodic trend of the elements. a. How is effective nuclear charge related to the atomic number of an element? b. Explain how shielding affects effective nuclear charge. c. In which direction (left to right or top to bottom in the periodic table) does effective nuclear charge generally increase and why? d. How does effective nuclear charge affect the size of the atom, ionization potential and electronegativity of the element?

19. Elements in the periodic table are primarily divided into metals, metalloid and nonmetals on the basis of metallic properties of the elements. a. Which groups of elements in the periodic table are known for their non-metallic character, and why? d. How does the number of valence electrons influence the metallic character of an element? e. Transition metals are used for making wire. why?
